subject: "scaled.shifted" mean and variance adjusted test statistic

messages.author: 5c527df876dd0445
messages.subject: "scaled.shifted" mean and variance adjusted test statistic
parts:
Hi,

What is the origin of the "scaled.shifted" mean and variance adjusted test statistic? According to lavaan help file, it is based on a test also implemented in Mplus 6 or higher. I just wonder where could I find the formulas to calculate it -- I just want to understand it better.

Thanks!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: "scaled.shifted" mean and variance adjusted test statistic
parts: What is the origin of the "scaled.shifted" mean and variance adjusted test statistic? According to lavaan help file, it is based on a test also implemented in Mplus 6 or higher. I just wonder where could I find the formulas to calculate it -- I just want to understand it better.

Look for the Satorra (2000) reference on the ?lavTestLRT help page.  There is also an Mplus Web Note (10) that discusses the details for the scaled-shifted chi-squared difference test, but the principles are the same as for the overall fit statistic (which implicitly compares the hypothesized model to a saturated model).

https://www.statmodel.com/download/webnotes/webnote10.pdf

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
